subject: Multilingual pilot: EU/APAC fit & next steps
messages:
From: Emma Lin <emma@lumenhealth.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
Cc: eng@lumenhealth.com
Date: 2026-11-25T08:42:00-08:00
Subject: Next steps after today's discovery call

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the call — that was helpful to align on the multilingual requirements. Quick recap from our side and what we'd need to see to move a pilot forward: 

- Primary languages: DE, FR, NL (EU) and JA, KO (APAC). We will also need light coverage for VI and TL as edge cases.
- Priority features: medical note summarization (sensitive PHI filtering), domain-specific QA, and high-fidelity translation-aware summarization.
- Success criteria: 1) F1/ROUGE targets per language (we have internal dev sets), 2) latency under 600ms P95 for single-doc summarization, 3) no increase in hallucination rate beyond our baseline.

What we'd like from you: model recommendations for EU vs APAC workloads, a prompt set we can run locally against our dev data, a short benchmark (N=500 per major language), and a proposed pilot scope/cost estimate.

Can you send a concise package (model recs + prompts + bench links) and an A/B plan for how Redwood would detect regressions during the pilot? We have procurement review the week of Dec 7, so aiming to sign a pilot early December if the package looks good.

—Emma
Emma Lin
Head of ML Infrastructure, LumenHealth
From: olga_petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Lin <emma@lumenhealth.com>
Cc: sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-26T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Next steps after today's discovery call

Hi Emma — great to talk yesterday. Below is a concise pilot package we discussed (attached assets + links). I put owners on the action items and included a short risk note about multilingual regressions.

Executive summary:
- Proposed pilot: 6-week focused evaluation across DE/FR/JA/KO with light runs for NL/VI/TL. Redwood will provide: model candidates, a prompt pack for summarization and PHI-safe redaction, benchmark tooling (scripts + expected outputs), and a regression-watch dashboard tied to prompt sets.

Recommended model matrix (initial candidates):
- EU primary: Llama-2-13b-chat (quant-4bit) — strong generalization on Germanic and Romance languages; best latency/quality tradeoff for summarization.
- EU fallback: Mistral-7b-instruct (float16) — lower footprint, useful for batch scoring and reranking.
- APAC primary: Mixtral-8x7B (chat-optimized) — better for JA/KO morphology and tokenization; we recommend quant-8bit for latency.
- Low-resource edge: BLOOMZ-7b1-mt for VI/TL tests (masking + cross-lingual transfer).

What you'll get (attachments & links):
- lumen_pilot_prompt_pack_v1.zip — prompt templates for summarization, redaction patterns, evaluation prompts for hallucination checks.
- eu-apac-benchmarks-202611.csv — baseline metrics we will generate for your dev sets (schema: lang, doc_id, reference, model_output, rouge, f1_ans, hallucination_flag).
- pilot-scope-matrix.xlsx — 6-week timeline, checkpoints, owners, expected compute.
- Shared readout link: https://drive.redwood.ai/benchmarks/LUM-4782/eu-apac-readout

Quality/regression controls (watchlist):
- Prompt drift: we will lock a canonical prompt set and report prompt-modified delta weekly.
- Tokenization mismatch: for JA/KO we will run tokenization parity checks; if subword OOV spikes > 2x, we pivot to model variant with alternative tokenizer.
- Hallucination regression: our evaluation harness flags candidate outputs with low overlap to reference and high hallucination_score; we will set an alert if hallucination rate increases by >5 percentage points vs baseline.

Costs & pilot estimate:
- Baseline run (6 weeks, 500 docs per major language, N=4 model variants) — estimated compute + infra: ~$12k (draft) — detailed pricing in pilot-scope-matrix.xlsx.

Action items (owners):
- Redwood: run initial bench on LU internal dev set (Sergio) — target Dec 2 for first pass.
- Redwood: upload prompt pack + bench scripts (Olga) — by Nov 29.
- LumenHealth: share sample dev sets + any additional POI redaction rules (Emma) — by Nov 30.
- Redwood/Procurement sync: prepare SOW + pilot agreement (Ben) — draft by Dec 3.

Risk notes:
- Domain mismatch on medical abbreviations may temporarily inflate hallucination flags; recommend a short token-level whitelist/blacklist we can import into the harness.
- Regulatory: since notes contain PHI, we will run everything in a private tenancy for the pilot (Redwood Dedicated) and redact where necessary; procurement should confirm scope.

If agreeable, I'll schedule a 30-minute kickoff for Dec 6 to align on data handoff and access.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
To: olga_petrov <olga@redwood.ai>, Emma Lin <emma@lumenhealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-27T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Next steps after today's discovery call

Appending some technical notes on the eval harness and data needs so we have a clear checklist before runs: 

- Dev set formatting: prefer JSONL with fields {id, language, text, reference_summary, pii_mask}. If you cannot export pii_mask, send a sample of 200 docs with obvious PHI flagged and we'll bootstrap heuristics.
- Tokenization parity: I'll run tokenization histograms (subword length distribution) for your JA/KO docs and compare to our model tokenizers. If we see >15% dev docs with >1.5x median token growth, expect latency impact.
- Evaluation metrics: We'll run ROUGE-L, F1 span-answer for extracted facts, and our internal hallucination_score (lexical novelty + factuality heuristics). A more conservative pass will include a human spot-check of 20 docs per language.
- CI/regression: We will create a baseline branch in the harness; new commits that change prompt templates will trigger an automated regression job. Alerts are configurable to Slack/email.

Estimate for initial runs: full pass across DE/FR/JA/KO (~2k docs) will take ~36 GPU hours on p4-class hardware. We can stage runs to prioritize DE/JA first if you want earlier readouts.

I'll start the tokenization checks as soon as you share formats.

—Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Applied ML, Redwood Inference

Speak soon — Emma
